 How Ryan Wedding Evaded Authorities for So Long 
 Accused drug kingpin allegedly had help from cartel leader, gangster 
 By 
 Arden Dier 
 with Newser.AI 
 Posted Nov 11, 2026 6:25 AM CST 
 Copied 
 Ryan Wedding, a former Canadian Olympic snowboarder facing charges related to drug trafficking and the killing of a federal witness, is taken off a plane at Ontario International Airport in Ontario, Calif. on Friday, Jan. 23, 2026.   (FBI via AP) 
 See 3 more photos 
 The Canadian snowboarder-turned-accused cartel boss who stayed a step ahead of authorities in Mexico for a decade allegedly had some powerful help. A newly unsealed US indictment says Mexican cartel leader Edgar Aaron "The General" Vazquez Alvarado supplied Ryan Wedding and co-conspirators with genuine police IDs, doctored to show their own names, and a rotating code word that let cocaine shipments glide past security forces, reports the CBC . Entry into Vazquez's inner circle allegedly cost Wedding $500,000 up front and about $100,000 a month. 
 Prosecutors also say Los Angeles gang figure Roberto "Fat Boy" Gomez funneled law-enforcement intel to Wedding, who was likely tipped off about numerous attempts to capture him before his January arrest . Gomez is a fugitive, believed to be in Mexico, per KNBC . Vazquez was killed by Mexican security forces last week and Wedding, who has pleaded not guilty to murder, money laundering, and drug-trafficking charges, is in US custody awaiting trial in Los Angeles. The case has also ensnared a Mexican judge, arrested last week in Colombia, who's accused of accepting a $2 million bribe to free Wedding's right-hand man from custody in February 2025, per the CBC . Andrew Clark was arrested again soon after and reportedly turned FBI informant .
